newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares edge down by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares edge down by lunch break.

text.p: Jakarta shares edged down during Thursday's morning session on profit-taking, with foreign players mainly on the sidelines, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index was off 0.10 points, or 0.01 percent, to 694.78 points after touching 696.25 points.In the broader market, however, gainers lead losers by 62 to 38 with 44 counters unchanged.
"Local players dominated the morning session speculating in second and third line stocks," a broker with foreign firm said.
Brokers said the market had shrugged off the news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
"There is no significant factor to spur foreign buying. I think Jakarta remains in a consolidation period after touching a record high last week," a foreign broker said.
Brokers said the market was likely to continue flat in the afternoon session as many foreign investors were sidelined for technical reason.

Thirdliner property firm Elang Realty was the most active stock with 13.7 million shares traded. It was up 22.22 percent to close the morning at 825 rupiah on speculation that a domestic conglomerate would buy stake in the firm through a tender offer.

Spring producer Indospring topped the gainers list with a 36 percent rise, up 625 rupiah to 2,350 rupiah on a volume of 1.5 million shares following market talk that a politically well connected businessman might take over the firm.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Garment firm Karwell was also actively traded, rising 50 rupiah to 1,375 rupiah on a volume of 7.1 million shares.
"It was boosted by market talk that it planned to issue convertible bonds and a rights issue," a local broker said.
Shares of engineering firm Bukaka shed 6.41 percent to 1,825 rupiah in active trading on profit-taking after the World Bank clarified that it did not give projects but loans.
Its shares soared on Wednesday on belief that it had received fresh projects.
Tin miner Tambang Timah was off 50 rupiah to 4,075 rupiah on continued profit-taking after falling to a low of 3,975 rupiah.
Timah has gone through sharp corrections since news of the division of the Busang gold project, in which it had said it was interested in participating.
